dedupe_keys.name: lidar based tree models for munich germany 2022

description: Markus Münzinger and the Leibniz Institute of Ecological Urban and Regional Development publish urban tree models for Munich from LiDAR observations acquired in February 2022. Registered descriptive metadata includes tree positions, heights and crown diameters, crown convex hulls and CityGML LoD2 vegetation objects. The reconstruction uses a canopy-height model at a 0.5-metre grid and vegetation above two metres. Geometric primitives represent individual crowns. The metadata states a role in spatial simulations of urban green infrastructure, and TUM2TWIN lists the models as vegetation for its city environment. The release is a historical Munich time slice, distinct from the corresponding 2012 resource. Files require registration at the IOER Research Data Centre. CC BY 4.0 reuse terms and restricted-access metadata both apply; a public description does not prove unrestricted file access or absence of charges. Caveats include automated reconstruction, approximate crown geometry and incomplete evidence on current vegetation. CityGML access is described through an archive link, which was not retrieved. The record relates to the aggregate TUM2TWIN benchmark and the 2012 tree models.
